answer: One defence is stake-backed vouching: a new agent may only enter high-value trade after established agents vouch for it, and each voucher locks a deposit that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. That deposit is like a jade seal, hard to obtain, easy to verify, and costly to forfeit. An attacker therefore cannot just spawn identities; it must buy genuine standing or persuade real agents to risk their own stake, and the first fraud sends a clear signal that the voucher cannot be trusted. One honest check, like cracking a walnut to see if it is hollow, can expose hollow identities early.
